title: Three corrections from an external audit: the 2051 count, the audited share, and the crossing years
summary: An external audit of the live site found three defects and all three are fixed here. /national/ published 93 local authorities below a 50% White British share by 2051 where the homepage and the finding said 86: that page kept its own inline filter from April and was missed by the commit that carried the v8.0 recalibration through every other surface, so it counted Sheffield under both its retired and its current code and counted the six London boroughs whose projection the plausibility guard withholds. It now reads the shared helper, and the test that checks the count on each page now checks every page that prints it rather than three of them. The true cost article described the audited portion of the £7,973M central estimate as "about 60%"; its own table puts £4,363M on an audited basis, which is 55%, and audited plus attributed is 63%. Both figures are now stated, derived from the cost categories and asserted against them. Threshold years for the Lancashire towns shipped as bare years and now carry a sensitivity band from the model's measured out-of-sample error: Blackburn 2026 to 2028, Pendle 2033 to 2035, Preston 2035 to 2039, Burnley 2048 to 2053. The homepage hotel headline now names the year it covers, because a 2024/25 average sat undated above figures from the latest quarter.

title: Home Office spending ledger, and the tribunal, route, small boats and hotel refresh behind it
summary: All 402 Home Office "spending over £25,000" transparency files from 2010 to 2026 are now ingested, and /what-the-home-office-publishes/ sets what the department publishes as transactions against what it reports as audited outturn. Asylum is tagged in two fields rather than one: filtering on Expense Area alone gives £2.85bn and misses £1.47bn, because the directorate label vanishes between 2017 and 2020 while the expense type codes do not. Every figure carries a basis, and two bases may be compared side by side with both named but never summed into one total. Tribunal appeal outcomes, route data, the weekly small boats series and the hotel and money ledgers were refreshed on 31 August and 4 September.

title: Model v8.0: recalibrated on an out-of-sample test, and the counts that follow from it
summary: The projection model was re-fitted and tested by fitting cohort change ratios on Census 2001 to 2011, forecasting 2021, and scoring against the actual Census 2021, so the fitting window never touches the target. On the White British share it scores mean absolute error 1.56pp with a bias of +0.05pp across 285 areas. The settings it replaces scored 2.82pp with a bias of -2.13pp on the same test, meaning the previous model projected change too fast rather than too slow. Shrinkage toward the national ratio is K=25 and the growth ceiling is 1.65 per decade, both chosen on that test. Counts move with it: 86 local authorities are projected below a 50% White British share by 2051 rather than 109, 59 of them currently majority, and Birmingham's 2051 share is 14.9% rather than 10.7%. The backcast comparison with NEWETHPOP is withdrawn; the defensible comparison is out-of-sample against out-of-sample, this model at 1.56pp across 285 areas against NEWETHPOP at 3.95pp across 296. Only a one-decade horizon has been tested.

title: Estate design system, five claim corrections, and a data refresh that had been failing since July
summary: The site moved onto the shared visual system used across the network. Five published claims were corrected: the 190,809 safe-and-legal humanitarian grants for year ending March 2026 are 77 per cent in-country extensions rather than arrivals, and out-of-country grants fell from 58,459 to 43,620; the 107,003 people in supported accommodation was the 31 December 2025 quarter end, not the current 97,519 at 31 March 2026, and it had been understating every area's share by about 9 per cent; and the claim that 70 nationalities see grant rates rise after appeal was never right, the figure being 101 of 105. Separately, the scheduled data refresh had failed on every run since at least 13 July, across five distinct faults, and now runs Monday and Thursday and deploys what it commits.

title: Small boats weekly series refreshed to 20 August 2026
summary: The Home Office weekly time series was 17 days past its own publication cadence and had been left behind by a refresh job that never included it. Now current to 20 August 2026.

title: Tribunal appeal outcomes updated to January to March 2026
summary: MOJ tribunal statistics for Q4 2025/26, covering January to March 2026 in the First-tier Tribunal Immigration and Asylum Chamber. These are financial-year quarters and are not interchangeable with the calendar quarters used for Home Office claims, decisions and support elsewhere on this site. Next edition 10 September 2026, covering April to June 2026.

title: Immigration system statistics, year ending March 2026
summary: The Home Office quarterly release. Routes, claims, decisions, backlog, support and returns updated to the year ending March 2026, with the accommodation snapshot at 31 March 2026.

title: Model v7.0: Census 2011 DC2101EW, per-LA migration, 25 findings
summary: Major model upgrade. Census 2011 DC2101EW (18 groups, observed) replaces NEWETHPOP proportional splitting. MAE improved 2.45 to 1.71pp. Per-LA ethnic migration rates from Census 2021. Scenario selector on every place page. Cost calculator. Backlog clock. Postcode resolver. Grant rate appeal toggle. 25 findings live. Withdrawn 13 August 2026: the 1.71pp was a backcast that fitted its ratios on the same two Censuses it was then scored against, so it measured the model's guardrails rather than its accuracy, and its bias ran the opposite way to the truth. The figures above are recorded as reported at the time and should not be quoted. Superseded by v8.0 on 23 August 2026.

title: Asy_D04 outcome analysis: true grant rates after appeals
summary: Home Office outcome analysis (Dec 2025) integrated. 103 nationalities with initial + appeal-adjusted grant rates. Average uplift +14.1pp. Iran 67% initial to 85% after appeals. Sri Lanka 27% to 59%.

title: ONS Births 2024 fertility data integrated
summary: Empirical TFRs from ONS Linked Births 2024. White British TFR 1.31, Pakistani 2.52. National ASFRs by age band. IMD deprivation fertility gradient 1.66x. 567,460 births analysed.
